title: Within-family heritability estimates for behavioural and disease phenotypes from 500,000 sibling pairs of diverse ancestries
title_zh: 来自50万名不同族裔兄弟姐妹对的行为和疾病表型的家族内遗传率估计
abstract: Quantification of the direct effect of genetic variation on human behavioural traits is important for understanding between-individual variation in socioeconomic and health outcomes but estimates of their heritability can be biased by between-family indirect genetic effects. By contrast, using within-family variation in DNA sharing is robust to most confounding factors including shared environmental effects and population stratification. Yet, accurate estimates for most traits are not available using this design, and none for non-European ancestry populations. Here we analyse approximately 500,000 sibling pairs with diverse genetic ancestries and obtain within-family heritability estimates for 14 phenotypes, including two well-studied model traits: height (0.70 ± 0.03) and BMI (0.49 ± 0.03). For behaviour, we find significant within-family heritability for smoking initiation (0.34 ± 0.05), alcohol consumption (0.18 ± 0.04), number of children (0.27 ± 0.11) and personality (‘talk versus listen’, 0.48 ± 0.13). In addition, we estimated large heritability for type 2 diabetes (0.43 ± 0.06) and asthma (0.34 ± 0.06), whose risk factors include behavioural traits. Overall, we show concordant estimates across ancestry groups and highlight a significant contribution of shared environmental effects for behaviour and type 2 diabetes risk, which may have inflated between-family estimates. Altogether, our results provide within-family evidence that genetic variation is associated with variation in complex traits, common disease and exposures. Our heritability estimates are concordant across genetic ancestries, lower than those from twin-based studies, yet larger than has been accounted for by genome-wide association studies so far. Using the variation in DNA sharing between 500,000 sibling pairs with diverse genetic ancestries, Yengo et al. estimate the heritability of 14 complex traits.
abstract_zh: 量化遗传变异对人类行为特征的直接影响，对于理解个体间在社会经济和健康结果中的变异至关重要，但其遗传率估计可能因家族间间遗传效应而产生偏差。相比之下，利用DNA共享的家族内变异对大多数混杂因素（包括共享环境效应和种族分层）具有鲁棒性。然而，大多数性状的这种设计下的准确估计尚不可用，更别提非欧洲裔人群了。在这里，我们分析了约50万对不同遗传族裔的兄弟姐妹，并获得了14种表型的家族内遗传率估计，包括两种研究较充分的模型性状：身高（0.70 ± 0.03）和BMI（0.49 ± 0.03）。在行为方面，我们发现吸烟起始（0.34 ± 0.05）、饮酒（0.18 ± 0.04）、生育子女数量（0.27 ± 0.11）以及人格特质（‘说话 versus 倾听’，0.48 ± 0.13）具有显著的家族内遗传率。此外，我们估计了2型糖尿病（0.43 ± 0.06）和哮喘（0.34 ± 0.06）的大遗传率，其风险因素包括行为特征。总体而言，我们展示了不同族裔群体之间的一致性估计，并强调了行为和2型糖尿病风险中共享环境效应的显著贡献，这可能夸大了家族间估计。总之，我们的研究结果提供了家族内证据，表明遗传变异与复杂性状、常见疾病和暴露变异有关。我们的遗传率估计在遗传族裔之间一致，低于基于双胞胎的研究，但目前基因组关联研究所能解释的要大。利用50万对不同遗传族裔兄弟姐妹的DNA共享变异，Yengo等人估计了14种复杂性状的遗传率。
